God had given him the strength to run in front of Ahab’s chariot. God had started a reformation in Israel through this man. “What are you doing here, Elijah?” echoed the words of the Lord in the prophet’s heart.

29th day, Tammuz, Year 20, morning I decided not to tell anyone except a few of the men I brought with me about my plans for last night. We got up at midnight to inspect the city. It’s even worse than I thought. I went out through the Valley Gate and rode toward the Dragon Well and the Trash Gate. These are all broken down. Fire has destroyed the gates. Then I rode toward the Fountain Gate and the King’s Pool. There wasn’t even enough room for me to get through on my horse, so I went through the valley and inspected the wall. So many gaps! I almost get sick when I think about how our beautiful city has been neglected. This is going to take a lot of work, but God will be with us. After we came back, I spent the rest of the night praying.
Later
Everybody—people, priests, nobles, officials—wants to help! I told them what God has done so far and how King Artaxerxes helped me. When I finished they said, “Let us start rebuilding!” And they did. They put on their work clothes, and got their tools, and we got started TODAY!
Of course Sanballat, Tobiah, and their new partner in crime, Geshem the Arab, heard about what we’re trying to do. They tried to accuse me of treason (they know nothing about my close relationship with the king). I tried to ignore them. No way are they going to stop me! God will give us success.

b.e: “I think we should each bring Him a gift,” said the first. “I will bring Him gold.”
b.x: “Acho que devemos cada um trazer-lhe um presente,” disse o primeiro. “Eu lhe trarei ouro.”

b.e: “That’s a good idea. I could bring Him some of my aromatic myrrh,” proposed a second wise man.
b.x: “É uma boa ideia. Eu poderia trazer-lhe um pouco da minha mirra aromática”, propôs um segundo sábio.

b.e: “Well, then I will bring some of my prized frankincense,” said another one.
b.x: “Bem, então eu trarei um pouco do meu incenso precioso,” disse outro.

b.e: Unbeknown to these men, each one of their gifts had a significance related to Jesus’ life. The gift of gold symbolized His royal origins from David’s lineage as well as His eternal rulership as the King of kings. Because myrrh was used to embalm the dead for burial, such a gift prefigured Jesus’ death as sacrifice for our sins. Frankincense was used in the Temple by the priests, so it would symbolize Jesus’ role as our High Priest who intercedes for the forgiveness of our sins.
b.x: Sem que esses homens soubessem, cada um de seus presentes tinha um significado relacionado à vida de Jesus. O presente de ouro simbolizava Sua origem real da linhagem de Davi, bem como Seu governo eterno como o Rei dos reis. Como a mirra era usada para embalsamar os mortos para o enterro, tal presente prenunciava a morte de Jesus como sacrifício pelos nossos pecados. O incenso era usado no Templo pelos sacerdotes, então simbolizaria o papel de Jesus como nosso Sumo Sacerdote que intercede pelo perdão de nossos pecados.

b.e: After the necessary preparations for the journey, the Wise Men saddled their camels and left to find the newborn King. The star that they first saw at the time Jesus was born would guide them by night. For many weeks and months the travelers patiently followed the star. At last they saw the golden dome of the Temple in Jerusalem. They made their way into town with great anticipation. “Where is the new King of the Jews?” they asked excitedly. Their inquiries were met by blank, confused looks.
b.x: Depois dos preparativos necessários para a viagem, os Sábios montaram seus camelos e partiram para encontrar o Rei recém‑nascido. A estrela que eles viram pela primeira vez no momento em que Jesus nasceu os guiaria à noite. Por muitas semanas e meses os viajantes seguiram pacientemente a estrela. Por fim, viram o domo dourado do Templo em Jerusalém. Eles se dirigiram à cidade com grande expectativa. “Onde está o novo Rei dos judeus?” perguntaram animadamente. Suas perguntas foram recebidas com olhares vazios e confusos.

b.e: But there are two more dreams and two more journeys in this story. When Herod realized that the visitors were not coming back through Jerusalem, he started plotting evil. b.e: By trusting God’s care and guidance, Joseph was able to lead Mary and Jesus to safety in Egypt, far from Herod and his evil schemes. God would let them know when the danger was past, and would guide them back home to Nazareth.
